newsitem.title: MEXICO: Human rights violations in Mexico said rising.
newsitem.headline: Human rights violations in Mexico said rising.

text.p: A joint French-Mexican human rights mission on Wednesday charged that suspected guerrilla sympathisers were arbitrarily arrested in Mexico and then tortured into confessing.

The French group Working Together for Human Rights and the Mexican League for the Defence of Human Rights said human rights abuses have soared since January 1994, and noted some particularly flagrant cases since the emergence in June of a new leftist guerrilla band calling itself the Popular Revolutionary Army (ERP).

The rights groups, which just concluded a two-month tour of some of Mexico's most violent states -- Guerrero, Chiapas, Oaxaca and Veracruz -- told a news conference that the army and federal and state Judicial Police were the worst human rights offenders.
"Since the appearance of the Popular Revolutionary Army, what we've had is a war also against social and political organisations that act peacefully," Steven Johansson of the French group said.

There was no immediate official reaction to the groups' accusations, but the government has repeatedly given assurances that individual rights would be protected while authorities hunted down the EPR.
A 20-page report issued by the two groups said on Aug. 21 their representatives interviewed eight men in an Acapulco prison who were arrested on suspicion of links to the EPR.

"They all alleged that they were tortured by the Mexican army during the first days of their detention," the report said, adding the torture claims were supported by scars on the bodies of the prisoners.
The groups also criticised the government for trampling on the rights of grass-roots peasants groups that officials allege are tied to the rebels.
Johansson said human rights violations in Mexico rose following the emergence of the unrelated Zapatista guerrilla force in southeastern Chiapas state in January 1994.
